value.coverage: Following those renames transitively and checking the target exists on disk: 107 of the 130 distinct unresolvable addresses resolve to their current home — 342 of the 378 occurrences. 82% of addresses and 90% of occurrences, with ZERO hand entries.
value.git_holds: 444 distinct file renames in the repo's history (git log --diff-filter=R -M -C).
value.so: The hand-authored table is not the cheap option and never was. 465 hand entries would have been 465 chances to mistype a fact git records perfectly, to cover 90% of what a derivation covers for free — and would still have needed a hand for the same two dissolutions.
value.the_residue_is_one_shape: 21 of the 23 git cannot resolve are DIRECTORIES (cairn/base, cairn/librarian, cairn/ground_loop, cairn/trouble, chart, ...). git tracks files, not directories, so a directory has no rename record by construction — and its move is nevertheless derivable from its files': if every tracked file under cairn/base/ now lives under cairn/tools/base/, the directory moved, and that is a consensus over the file record, not a new source of truth. The genuine leftovers are TWO: cairn/base/state.json and cairn/chart/intention+why.json, both files that did not move but DISSOLVED — and a dissolution is exactly the case that should need a hand to say where the intent went.

value.CC_does_not_have_a_recommendation_and_th: Both readings survive the charter. The sieve docstring — 'a promoted build must still match what its packet charted' — is true of either, because the two readings were never distinguished when it was written. Choosing here would be CC settling a spec question by reading the implementation back as intent, which is the one direction the record says not to reason in.
value.question: What is the invariant these three sieves are supposed to enforce — 'every chart this component EVER made still resolves', or 'the chart of the voyage being promoted still resolves'?
value.reading_A_every_chart_ever: The gate asserts the whole historical record stays navigable: any packet ever berthed against this component still points at real files. STRONGEST claim, and it means a bulk move must forward EVERYTHING or the corpus stays red forever. It is also the reading under which the derivation below is not an optimisation but a requirement, because a hand can not keep up with the corpus's own rate of movement.
value.reading_B_the_promoting_voyage: The gate asserts only that the build being promoted RIGHT NOW matches the chart that authorized it. Narrower, and it is the 2026-07-24 failure's actual shape ('done' reported while THOSE files stood unmoved). Under it, most of the 306 are not findings at all — they are old charts of finished voyages, and the gate should not be re-judging them. THE COST OF THIS READING, stated plainly so it is not chosen by accident: the historical record stops being checked, and a chart from a year ago pointing at nothing becomes ordinary rather than red.
value.what_was_checked_before_asking_and_what_: The charter was read first, and it narrows the question rather than answering it. build_inspector's charter divides three seats in one sentence — 'Entry gates the door, promotion judges the middle, exit measures the close' — and says of promotion: 'Promotion judges a build AGAINST its chart.' Singular, possessive: that is reading B, and it settles what the SEAT is for. What it does not settle is which packets the sweep READS, and the same charter is why: `inspect()` with no component is 'the whole-repo sweep', which has no current build at all, so under a strict reading B these three sieves would have nothing to say there — and they are in SIEVES, so they run there. The code loops over every orient packet the component ever berthed (`_charted_packets(comp_dir, 'orient')`), which is reading A. So the charter's words say B about the seat and the code says A about the corpus, and neither contradicts the other because the distinction was never drawn.
value.why_it_is_yours_and_not_CC's: It is not a code choice with a right answer in the corpus; it is what the gate is FOR, and the two readings build different things. CC will not settle it by picking the one that makes 306 findings go away — that is the disposition the 2026-08-14 rule forbids wearing a design argument's clothes.

value.read_downward: 215 calls between the packet and done. Roughly 60 of them are the three measurement instruments re-run (the three-way decomposition, the residue, the mutation sweep) and the four proof/inspector re-runs, which are the build's own evidence rather than looking behind the packet. The rest is the score.

value.a: 306 FINDINGS, ONE CAUSE, THREE SIEVE NAMES. Read as a count, this looks like the corpus is in trouble in three different ways. Read by address, it is one bulk move seen from three angles. A gate that reports the same cause 306 times has a naming problem as well as a forwarding problem, and the second is not fixed by fixing the first.

NOT ONE OF THESE CLAIMS WAS FALSE WHEN IT WAS WRITTEN. That is what separates this whole class from the 2026-07-24 failure the sieves were built for. There, the claim was false at the moment it was made. Here, the claim was true and the world moved. The gate cannot currently tell those apart, and telling them apart is what the ruling above decides.

A HAND-AUTHORED FORWARDING TABLE IS A SECOND COPY OF A FACT THE REPOSITORY HOLDS. The mechanism is not wrong — it is right for the case it was built for (a deliberate move a build makes) and was reached for outside it. Aiming it at a bulk reorg asks a hand to re-derive what git recorded automatically, which is Law 1's defect with a data structure around it.

THE 82%/90% SPLIT IS THE ARGUMENT, NOT THE 100%. Derivation does not have to be complete to be right. It has to cover the mechanical bulk so that what is LEFT is small enough for a hand to answer honestly — and what is left here is two dissolutions, which is exactly the set that needs a human to say where the intent went.

THE UNIT IS THE (ADDRESS, TICKET) PAIR, AND THE TICKET SAID 'ADDRESS' EVERYWHERE. A forwarding order is one TICKET's record, so the same address is legitimately answered under one ticket and unanswered under another — cairn/chart/intention+why.json resolves under watchme-emits-a-probe's hand order and not at all for a claimless packet. Two hypotheses were KILLED on this one cause: both counted address occurrences, and address-level accounting can never close. The residue instrument had to be rebuilt around the pair before its numbers meant anything.

THE TWO DISSOLUTIONS THE CAST PREDICTED ARE ONE DISSOLUTION AT FIVE ADDRESSES. Counting events by address overcounts them. chart's twelve proofs went to eleven destinations — ten under builder/machines/<stage>/proofs, one each to tools/chain, tools/tree and skills/moreabout — so no plurality exists and the derivation correctly declines. skills/chart is the successor for the COMPONENT because its charter moved there whole; that is a fact only a hand holds, which is the hand door's whole reason to exist.

PLURALITY OVER UNANIMITY WAS MEASURED, NOT CHOSEN. 67 of base's 71 addresses answer under a strict-majority plurality against 64 under unanimity, and the three unanimity lost voted 6-1-1, 9-1 and 9-1. A bulk move is never unanimous — the stragglers move separately, later, in their own commits — so unanimity is a rule that reds precisely on the case the ticket was cast for.

THE MUTATION FOUND A TOOTH THE REVIEW HAD PASSED. Tooth (c) — 'a live address is never forwarded' — stayed green with the live-address guard deleted outright, because the fixture asked about a rename TARGET, which has no chain to follow: it was measuring git's silence rather than the resolver's refusal. Reading the proof could not see this; inverting the implementation could. The fixture now brings a name back from the dead. 6 of 6 seeded cases red on their own tooth and nothing else's.

THE THREE-WAY DECOMPOSITION IS THE MEASUREMENT, NOT THE BEFORE/AFTER. A single before/after cannot say which door did the work, so each door was disabled in turn: no door 362 findings across 9 components; hand door only 264 across 6; both doors 6 across 2; both doors plus the dissolution named by a hand, 0. Every per-sieve and per-component bucket falls monotonically. The cast's 82%/90% estimate was in the right neighbourhood for the wrong reason — it estimated over addresses.

WHAT IS LEFT IS NOT A HAND'S DEBT. Residue closed 17 pairs → 4, and the four are ONE claimless orient packet: a packet naming no ticket has no ticket whose forwarding order could answer for it. That is a structural floor of the pair-unit design, not an unwritten order, and it is owed its own ticket rather than an entry in someone's table.

THERE IS NO INTAKE DOOR FOR A TICKET'S `forwarding` FIELD. The thirteen hand entries that closed the dissolution were written by direct JSON edit across twelve tickets — one fact duplicated twelve times, with nothing checking either end at write time. The build checks both ends at READ time, which is why the entries are honest; nothing makes the next one honest.
